regions.label: Left outer hood
regions.evidence: Hood fabric is bounded by the outer silhouette, face edge and stitched neckline join. Recovered cell 35 continues the same fabric beside the drawcord; its partition does not establish another sewn panel.

regions.label: Right outer hood
regions.evidence: The face edge, crown division and stitched neckline delimit the matching outer hood half.

regions.label: Left inner hood panel
regions.evidence: Visible fabric inside the hood has a continuous center-back seam and curved side-panel join; it is not an empty neck opening.

regions.label: Right inner hood panel
regions.evidence: The center-back seam and curved side join delimit the matching visible interior hood fabric.

regions.label: Left inner hood side panel
regions.evidence: A narrow visible interior fabric panel lies between the hood face edge and a continuous curved join extending to the hood base.

regions.label: Right inner hood side panel
regions.evidence: The matching continuous curved interior join separates this narrow fabric surface from the central inner hood panel.

regions.label: Left hood drawcord
regions.evidence: Parallel cord outlines descend from the hood and terminate in a visibly enclosed knot and short end; these cells form one drawcord.

regions.label: Right hood drawcord
regions.evidence: The matching outlined cord, enclosed knot and projecting end are supported trim independent of hood fabric.

regions.label: Left upper chest and shoulder
regions.evidence: A continuous curved chest join with parallel dashed topstitching separates this upper section from the lower body. It extends uninterrupted to the dropped sleeve attachment.

regions.label: Right upper chest and shoulder
regions.evidence: The matching curved seam and adjacent topstitching establish a separate upper construction section, ending at the center closure and sleeve join.

regions.label: Left lower body
regions.evidence: Visible body fabric lies below the stitched curved chest join and above the hem-band seam. The recovered patch-pocket perimeter bounds a separate pocket, not a body fold.

regions.label: Right lower body
regions.evidence: The curved chest construction seam, side contour and hem join delimit this lower body surface, with the recovered visible pocket kept separate.

regions.label: Left main sleeve
regions.evidence: A stitched dropped-shoulder join starts the sleeve; its main surface is bounded by the outer contour and curved lower-sleeve insert seam.

regions.label: Right main sleeve
regions.evidence: The matching dropped-shoulder seam and curved insert join visibly delimit the main sleeve fabric.

regions.label: Left curved sleeve insert
regions.evidence: A long curved solid join accompanied by dashed topstitching separates this lower-sleeve insert from the main sleeve; it terminates at the cuff attachment.

regions.label: Right curved sleeve insert
regions.evidence: The matching curved seam has parallel topstitching and reaches the cuff, supporting an actual sewn sleeve insert rather than a wrinkle.

regions.label: Left front patch pocket
regions.evidence: The recovered surface has a stitched upper edge, curved hand-entry edge and stitched lower attachment. These are genuine patch-pocket construction boundaries.

regions.label: Right front patch pocket
regions.evidence: The matching recovered pocket face is enclosed by its top attachment, curved entry edge, lower stitching and center closure. No backing surface is added.

regions.label: Left hem band
regions.evidence: A stitched transverse attachment separates the band from the body; its lower edge is the garment hem and its inner end meets the zipper.

regions.label: Right hem band
regions.evidence: The matching lower band has its own stitched body attachment and free hem edge, divided from the opposite half by the front closure.

regions.label: Left cuff
regions.evidence: A transverse stitched seam joins the narrow cuff to the gathered sleeve end; the cuff has a separate closed outer outline.

regions.label: Right cuff
regions.evidence: The matching cuff is separated from the gathered sleeve by a stitched attachment seam.

excluded.reason: Tiny zipper-related enclosures do not reliably distinguish solid hardware from pull openings or gaps; left unfilled rather than treated as fabric.
Minute enclosures at closure and seam intersections are stitch or ink fragments, not independently editable garment components.
Tiny pocket-edge stitch/intersection fragments do not establish additional pocket surfaces or hardware.

warnings: The center-front zipper is visible, but no reliable continuous enclosed zipper surface is supplied; its tiny ambiguous cells remain unfilled.
Upper chest cells include uninterrupted shoulder extensions to the dropped sleeve joins. No additional shoulder or upper-sleeve cuts have been invented.
Only the recovered visible patch-pocket faces are classified; no hidden backing or body fabric behind them is supplied.
